new_statements.rule_in_words: Impressionistic word accent on the first syllable of the (written, prefix-included) word; frequently no audible prominence at all; a handful of lexical exceptions with accent on a later syllable are marked in bold in the entries (only four such markings occur in c. 3000 entries, e.g. ta-LAP, ki-velA, tshopI-e). No tone is recognised or marked.
new_statements.exceptions: 'often there is no accent distinguishable'; non-initial accent marked ad hoc in bold on four entries (ta-lap 'white marriage' with bold stem, ki-vela with bold final a, tshopi-e greeting with bold i, one plural form -meri).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms in a dictionary; 'initial syllable' evidently counts the noun-class/infinitive prefix as part of the word (since ta-LAP with stem accent is flagged as an exception), which is linguistically suspicious for a Temne-type language. Author is an art historian who explicitly disclaims linguistic training; trained-linguist sources disagree on whether the Baga lects are tonal (Childs 1995: 'likely' tonal like Temne; Seidel 2025: neighbouring Baga Mandori 'clearly tonal'; Rochant 2023: Baga group 'not known to be tonal'; Ganong 1998 via PHOIBLE: no tonemes). Treat as a placeholder pending Ganong 1998 / Diassi 1974.
new_statements.identity_note: Lamp's 'Baga tshi-Tem (Sitem/Sitemu)' = Baga Sitemu, baga1272/bsp, covering both descent-group dialects (Somtup and Bɔgləntsh villages: Kamsar, Katako, Tolkotsh, Kawass, etc.); his dictionary also includes flagged words from M'ndor (Baga Mandori, a separate Glottolog languoid), Kakissa, Koba and Kalum lects. Seidel 2025's tonal statement concerns Baga Mandori, not Sitemu. Glottolog subsumes Kakissa/Baga Sobané (Sané 1980) under bsp.

sources.citation: Lamp, Frederick John. 2021 [first posted 2016, revised June 2021]. Baga Tshi-Tem Dictionary (Guinea) / Po-lokuloku pə tshə-Baka tshi-Tem (c. 3000 Baga words). 132 pp. PDF posted on Cataloging Africana (WordPress), https://catalogingafricana.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/
sources.note: Front matter, heading 'Intonation' (PDF p. 7): 'The accent generally falls on the initial syllable, although often there is no accent distinguishable. When the accent falls on a following syllable, it is indicated in bold.' Only four entries in the whole dictionary carry such bold marking (e.g. ta-LAP 'white marriage', ki-velA 'hadada bird', tshopI-e 'greeting'). Author is an art historian who states he has 'no formal linguistic training'; no tone marked anywhere.

sources.citation: Rochant, Neige. 2023. A Bilectal Grammar of Baga Pukur: an Atlantic Language of Guinea. PhD thesis, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle. 1033 pp. https://theses.hal.science/tel-05618821
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Describes Baga Pukur (a different, non-Mel language), not Baga Sitemu. Only relevant remark, p. 229 (PDF p. 260): 'neighbouring Mel languages along the coast, such as the Baga group, are not known to be tonal.' Nothing on Sitemu stress placement. Bibliography names Soumah 1990 (Conakry MA comparing Sitemu/Mandori/Pukur noun classes) and Lamp 2016.
